label: Teaser
prompt:
TEASER | SHOT T01 | THE EMPTY HOUSE — BROKEN INSTRUMENT
DURATION: 15 SECONDS
FORMAT: HORIZONTAL 16:9
ONE CONTINUOUS HANDHELD TAKE


LOCATION REFERENCE

The sisters’ private room: {{LOC_PRIVATE_ROOM}}

Preserve the referenced architecture, doorway, furnishings,
plants, curtains, materials and warm domestic character.

The room remains empty of people.


PROP REFERENCE AND REQUIRED BROKEN STATE

The musician’s instrument: {{PROP_INSTRUMENT_BROKEN}}

Use the reference to preserve the instrument’s identity,
materials, proportions and decorative details.

Its required physical state is a severely broken instrument
lying in several separate pieces DIRECTLY ON THE ROOM FLOOR.

Show approximately four to six substantial fragments:
the split main soundbox,
the detached neck,
and several broken sections of its body.

Preserve recognizable parts of the same single instrument.
Jagged fractured edges and exposed inner surfaces make
the damage immediately readable.

Spread the pieces irregularly across approximately
80 centimeters of the floor, with visible floor between them.

The largest soundbox fragment lies on its side.
Its broken opening faces diagonally toward the camera.
The detached neck lies flat at a different angle nearby.
Smaller fragments rest separately around them.

Every piece is supported directly by the floor itself.
Their weight, contact shadows and resting angles clearly
establish floor contact.

The instrument is already broken at the first frame.
Its fragments remain in exactly the same positions throughout.

One loose string remains attached to a fragment.


STARTING COMPOSITION

The half-open entrance door occupies the RIGHT foreground.
The open gap lies between its free edge and the LEFT jamb.

Through the gap, reveal an empty chair in the LEFT middle distance,
plants deeper inside and part of a softly moving curtain.

The scattered instrument fragments lie on the floor approximately
1.5 meters beyond the threshold, just RIGHT of the initial sightline.

The door leaf initially conceals them.
The door remains at the same half-open angle throughout.

The camera gradually reveals the fragments through parallax.

The cat remains off-screen.
Visible spaces and furnishings remain unoccupied.


LIGHTING

Soft warm daylight enters through the established window.
Preserve the location reference’s natural light direction.

The corridor is dimmer than the room.
The foreground door edge forms a dark boundary around
the warm interior.

Light across the floor reveals the separate instrument fragments,
their broken edges and their individual contact shadows.

Keep the floor visible beneath and between the pieces.

Maintain consistent illumination and exposure throughout,
including during the final rapid camera movement.


CAMERA

One continuous shot with a 35mm lens.
Camera height approximately 45 centimeters above the floor.

Begin outside the room, looking through the half-open doorway.

The opening movement is slow and observant,
with subtle handheld breathing.

The final movement becomes abrupt, anxious and searching,
triggered by a distant off-screen cat sound.


00:00–00:05 — THE QUIET ROOM

Move very slowly forward toward the doorway.

The empty chair remains in the left middle distance.
Plants and warm domestic textures remain deeper inside.
The curtain moves slightly in a faint draft.

The foreground door still conceals the broken instrument.

Sound: quiet room tone and faint curtain movement.


00:05–00:11 — THE SCATTERED PIECES

Continue approximately 50 centimeters forward
and 20 centimeters LEFT through the doorway gap.

As the lens passes the door’s free edge,
gradually reveal the instrument fragments scattered
DIRECTLY ACROSS THE FLOOR.

Make a small downward tilt.

Frame the entire damaged arrangement:
the split soundbox on its side,
the detached neck lying flat,
and separate broken body sections around them.

Include a generous margin of bare floor around the fragments.
Keep visible floor gaps between the individual pieces.

The image must read immediately as the aftermath of an instrument
having been smashed and left where its pieces fell.

The camera slows as it discovers the damage.
Hold long enough for the separated pieces to register clearly.

All fragments remain motionless.
A faint draft shifts the end of one attached loose string,
producing a delicate metallic tick against a broken body section.


00:11–00:15 — THE ANXIOUS SEARCH

00:11–00:11.5:
Briefly hold on the scattered fragments.

One short, distant cat meow comes from OFF-SCREEN LEFT,
deeper inside the house.

00:11.5–00:12.2:
React immediately with a fast handheld pan LEFT,
approximately 50 degrees toward the sound.

The movement feels startled, worried and urgently attentive.

The broken pieces leave frame through the RIGHT edge.
They remain in their original positions on the floor.

Allow natural directional motion blur and a brief loss of focus.

00:12.2–00:13.5:
Overshoot slightly, then make a short corrective movement RIGHT.

Recover focus on an empty gap between the existing furnishings
near the curtain.

Keep the framing unsettled through small handheld shifts,
a slight horizon roll and a searching adjustment.

00:13.5–00:15:
Take one short, hesitant step forward through the clear floor space.

Angle the camera slightly farther LEFT,
trying to see beyond the existing foreground obstruction.

Reveal only more empty interior.

At exactly 15 seconds, cut directly to solid black
while the search remains unresolved.
Cut all sound to silence.


CONTINUITY

One instrument, already broken into several separate pieces.
All fragments lie directly on the floor.
Their positions, damage and materials remain constant.

The furniture and architecture remain fixed.
The door retains its original half-open angle.

The tension comes from discovering unmistakable physical damage
inside a quiet, otherwise ordinary home.


SOUND

Quiet room tone.
Faint curtain movement.
One delicate contact from the loose instrument string.
One distant, slightly muffled cat meow from the left.
Subtle clothing movement behind the camera during the rapid turn.
One soft footstep during the final searching advance.

Absolute silence at the final cut.

NO MUSIC. NO DIALOGUE.

Established requirements for this subject:
- No human appears without a mask. Every person on screen, including nobles, gift-bearers, servants and background figures, wears a mask. A figure who is not a named character takes one of the masked caste looks in REF-001, Civilization Caste Board. Never show a bare human face.

<<<image_1>>> is Jamshid Daughters Chamber (LOC-020 V01); match it wherever Jamshid Daughters Chamber appears.
<<<image_2>>> is Instrument Saz (PRP-018 V01); match it wherever Instrument Saz appears.
